speaker: Unknown
en: Well, thank you for joining.
zh: 好的，感谢各位的到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final day of the conference here.
zh: 这是会议的最后一天了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know it's been a long week, but I'm excited to talk about a topic here that is very near and dear to me, software factories.
zh: 我知道这一周很漫长，但我很期待聊一个我非常非常关心的话题，软件工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: This would probably not be a new concept to any of you.
zh: 这个概念对你们中的任何人来说可能都不算新。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm guessing if you're all here, you're very familiar with software factories.
zh: 我猜既然你们都在这里，你们对软件工厂已经非常熟悉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ramp blogged about their inspects several months ago.
zh: Ramp 几个月前在博客上写了他们的 inspects。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think maybe in December last year.
zh: 我想也许是去年 12 月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget exactly when.
zh: 我记不清具体时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a little while.
zh: 已经有一段时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that really kind of excited the entire industry of thinking, oh, we can actually build software very differently now that AI is extremely capable of writing code.
zh: 这真的让整个行业兴奋起来，开始思考：哦，既然 AI 已经极其擅长写代码，我们现在其实可以用非常不同的方式构建软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of other companies have followed suit.
zh: 很多其他公司也纷纷效仿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's kind of like a standard setup here.
zh: 而且这里大致有一套标准配置。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a sandbox that you put your code into.
zh: 你有一个沙箱，把你的代码放进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: You put an AI agent in there, maybe a Claude Code section or an open code.
zh: 你在里面放一个 AI 智能体，也许是 Claude Code 区块或者 open code。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with a prompt, it generates a PR and you merge it.
zh: 然后给一个提示词，它生成一个 PR,然后你把它合并。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might be building this already yourself.
zh: 你们可能已经自己在构建这个东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have taken a slightly different approach at WorkOS.
zh: 我们在 WorkOS 采取了一个稍微不同的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the motivation for what we are building is that we see a lot of the kind of success metrics really focusing on output, right?
zh: 我们构建它的动机是，我们看到很多所谓的成功指标其实都在聚焦产出，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you'll see posts on X and blogs talking about the percentage of PRs or the number of pull requests or how much code is being generated by AI moving into production.
zh: 比如你会看到 X 上的帖子或者博客，谈论 AI 生成的 PR 的百分比，或者 pull request 的数量，或者有多少 AI 生成的代码进入了生产环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is just really output metrics that this can actually disguise how well these systems are working.
zh: 而这些只是产出指标，它们实际上可能掩盖这些系统运行得好不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Percentage of PRs or number of PRs may belie an overall increase in PRs.
zh: PR 的百分比或者 PR 的数量可能掩盖了 PR 总量的整体上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to distinguish whether the output is actually driving outcomes.
zh: 很难区分产出是否真的在驱动成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's kind of where we focus our efforts when we're thinking about a software factory.
zh: 所以这就是我们思考软件工厂时聚焦的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like if we're going to go put engineering time into building this level of automations, and there's a bit of work that needs to go into this, full-time teams dedicated to this, how do we want to think about the success of this and whether this is actually driving value for our organization, our engineering organization?
zh: 就是说，如果我们要投入工程时间去构建这种级别的自动化，而这需要相当多的工作，需要全职团队专门投入其中，那我们应该如何思考它的成功与否，以及它是否真的在为我们的组织、我们的工程组织创造价值？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we measure instead of just code output, we're looking at outcome metrics.
zh: 所以我们衡量的不只是代码产出，我们看的是成果指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is really about like are we accelerating our ability to deliver features.
zh: 这真正关乎的是，我们是否在加速交付功能的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think that the dream of the software factory is that it gives each of our engineers a small engineering team for themselves.
zh: 我们认为软件工厂的梦想是，它给我们每一位工程师一个属于他们自己的小型工程团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the consequence of that really needs to be that we're building more and we're shipping more.
zh: 而这样做的后果，就应该是我们构建得更多、发布得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that as we embark on complex features, those can get built a lot more quickly.
zh: 而且当我们着手复杂功能时，那些功能能更快地被构建出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does this actually look like?
zh: 那么这实际上是什么样子的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we kind of started with the same thing you've seen in other factories.
zh: 嗯，我们最初做的事情和其他工厂里看到的大致一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It started with the sandbox we built on top of Cloudflare.
zh: 它始于我们基于 Cloudflare 构建的沙箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: We put an open code model router in there.
zh: 我们在里面放了一个 open code 模型路由器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're feeding it prompts.
zh: 我们给它喂提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we very quickly ran into this situation where this wasn't driving more outcomes.
zh: 而且我们很快就遇到了这样一种情况：这并没有带来更多成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was not an incremental increase or an exponential increase over engineers just driving Claude code on their laptops.
zh: 相比工程师们在自己的笔记本电脑上驱动 Claude code,这既不是渐进式的提升，也不是指数级的提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was actually pretty indistinguishable for us.
zh: 对我们来说，实际上几乎无法区分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we really kind of started to think about, well, how can we embed our engineering processes into the factory itself?
zh: 于是我们真正开始思考，好吧，我们怎样才能把我们的工程流程嵌入到工厂本身之中？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not sufficient that the factory is producing code.
zh: 工厂能产出代码是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually wanted to take a lot of the other work that our engineers do to produce products and automate that as well.
zh: 我们实际上想把工程师们为产出产品所做的很多其他工作也自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we kind of split this into two parts.
zh: 所以我们把它拆成了两个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is we have this system we call TARS.
zh: 一个是我们有一套叫 TARS 的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a way for users to interact with the coding agent.
zh: 这是用户与编码智能体交互的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is embedded into the tools that we use.
zh: 而且它嵌入在我们使用的工具之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So not just Slack, but also Linear and GitHub.
zh: 所以不只是 Slack,还有 Linear 和 GitHub。

speaker: Unknown
en: We subscribe to webhooks through TARS so that TARS can actually track the progress of projects in addition to generating the code outputs.
zh: 我们通过 TARS 订阅 webhook,这样 TARS 除了生成代码产出之外，还能实际跟踪项目的进度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we built a separate system called Horizon.
zh: 然后我们构建了另一套独立的系统，叫 Horizon。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the infrastructure orchestration layer.
zh: 这是基础设施编排层。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a lot more similar to Inspect and Minions and some of the other systems that other companies have built.
zh: 它和 Inspect、Minions 以及其他公司构建的一些其他系统要相似得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it sits in front of an MCP gateway.
zh: 但它位于一个 MCP 网关之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm going to talk a little bit more about why that MCP gateway has been really transformational for us.
zh: 我接下来会多讲一点,为什么这个 MCP 网关对我们来说真正具有变革性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So by feeding our web hooks activities that are happening in other source code systems and project tracking systems, we're starting to get to that level of autonomy where our factory is performing product engineering work, not just code work.
zh: 通过把其他源代码系统和项目跟踪系统中正在发生的活动以 webhook 的形式喂给它,我们开始达到那种自主性水平,我们的工厂在执行产品工程工作,而不仅仅是代码工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's an example of this?
zh: 那么这方面有什么例子呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: In linear, we can define tickets that have dependencies.
zh: 在 Linear 里,我们可以定义有依赖关系的工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one ticket blocks another ticket.
zh: 也就是一张工单阻塞另一张工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty common for breaking down large units of work into smaller ones.
zh: 这是把大的工作单元拆分成小的,很常见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because TARS is getting webhooks on ticket completion, it can automatically pick up the next ticket in a cycle.
zh: 因为 TARS 在接收工单完成的 webhook,它可以自动在一个循环中接手下一张工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we can, through our planning process, construct a map of how we think this plan is going to get executed, and TARS can start to execute on that autonomously.
zh: 这样我们就可以通过规划过程,构建一张我们认为这个计划将如何被执行的地图,而 TARS 可以开始自主地执行它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that we have is in between those steps, when a ticket is completed, we can ask TARS, can you reevaluate the linear project and let me know if it's missing now tickets?
zh: 另一件我们有的事情是,在这些步骤之间,当一张工单完成时,我们可以问 TARS,你能不能重新评估一下这个 Linear 项目,然后告诉我它现在是否缺少工单?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because as you do work, you're learning about where are the gaps in their plan.
zh: 因为在你做工作的过程中,你是在了解他们的计划里哪里有缺口。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we want to continuously keep our plan fresh by using the agent itself.
zh: 我们想通过使用智能体本身来持续保持我们的计划是新鲜的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The agent is determining that there may be missing pieces to what we initially planned for the project and the goal that we have in mind.
zh: 智能体在判断,相对于我们最初为项目和心中目标所做的规划,可能存在缺失的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we run this product engineering culture at WorkOS.
zh: 所以我们在 WorkOS 运行这种产品工程文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where engineers are responsible for a lot of the product functions.
zh: 在这里,工程师对很多产品职能负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have product managers on teams today.
zh: 我们今天的团队里没有产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the rituals as part of this product engineering process is we create a Hilltop document.
zh: 而这个产品工程流程的一个仪式是,我们会创建一份 Hilltop 文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a PRD, and it is intended to both define what is the purpose of this project, but also incorporate
zh: 它是一份 PRD,旨在既定义这个项目的目的是什么,同时也纳入

speaker: Unknown
en: What are our customers talking about?
zh: 我们的客户在谈论什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are we seeing the need for this unit of work?
zh: 我们在哪里看到对这一工作单元的需求?

speaker: Unknown
en: It looks at competitive analysis.
zh: 它会看竞品分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there similar products out in the market today that we can draw inspiration from?
zh: 如今市场上是否有类似的产品可以供我们汲取灵感?

speaker: Unknown
en: We start to bring early design screens into this, and we outline what are the major milestones.
zh: 我们开始把早期设计稿带进来,并勾勒出主要里程碑是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so by kind of consolidating and canonicalizing this information into a document, this is something our product engineers have been doing throughout the entire company.
zh: 通过把这些信息整合并规范化成一份文档,这是我们的产品工程师在整个公司一直在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we can give this resource to an agent, and an agent can break this into units of work.
zh: 现在我们可以把这个资源给一个智能体,一个智能体可以把它拆分成工作单元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this has been a really powerful way for us to take existing processes and encode them into the factory themselves.
zh: 所以这一直是我们把现有流程编码进工厂本身的一种非常强大的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I mentioned, it's listening for webhooks.
zh: 就像我提到的,它在监听 webhook。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll show an example of what this looks like.
zh: 我会展示一个例子,看看这是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it can see that the Hilltop document, through linear tickets, has been reviewed and approved, and by virtue of it being approved, can start work on this project automatically.
zh: 但它可以看到,Hilltop 文档通过 Linear 工单已被审阅并批准,而凭借它被批准这一点,就可以自动开始这个项目的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we don't need a human to be shepherding this agent through every single step of the life cycle.
zh: 所以我们不需要一个人在整个生命周期的每一步都在牧羊式地引导这个智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we created an agent specifically for this part of the process.
zh: 所以我们专门为流程的这个部分创建了一个智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it the PM.
zh: 我们叫它 PM。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it is doing the first draft of the Hilltop based on the brief specification that we give it.
zh: 它基于我们给它的简短规格说明,起草 Hilltop 的初稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's adding context to that in addition to reading the human reviews.
zh: 它在此之上补充上下文,另外还要阅读人类的审阅意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it picks up the implementation and breaking that into tickets.
zh: 然后它接手实现工作,并将其拆分成工单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's an opportunity for humans to stay in the loop for each part of this process.
zh: 而且在这个流程的每个部分,人类都有机会保持在循环中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's very common for a human to intervene or comment on a ticket that's generated by AI, give it further guidance or refinement.
zh: 我是说,人类对 AI 生成的工单进行干预或评论、给它进一步的指导或细化,是非常常见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's really about that cold start problem where we can kind of get over the hump of creating all these different resources.
zh: 但这真正是关于那个冷启动问题,我们可以有点儿翻过创建所有这些不同资源这道坎。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK, so what does this actually look like?
zh: 好,那么这实际看起来是什么样子?

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's a project I kicked off last month, two months ago.
zh: 这是我上个月、两个月前启动的一个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're adding a new API to a product I lead called Vaults.
zh: 我们在为我负责的一个叫 Vaults 的产品添加一个新的 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with a command here in Slack, I can kick off this project with a simple description, usually a few sentences, of what I'm trying to accomplish.
zh: 通过 Slack 里的一条命令,我可以启动这个项目,只带一个简单的描述,通常是几句话,说明我想完成什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: TARS then goes in and creates all these resources for me.
zh: TARS 然后进去为我创建所有这些资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't need to go and create the project in linear.
zh: 我不需要去在 Linear 里创建项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't need to create a draft of the Notion document, all of the decision logs and the open questions.
zh: 我不需要创建 Notion 文档的草稿、所有的决策日志和开放问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: TARS is creating a first pass at that.
zh: TARS 在为这些做初稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this then gives me an easy framework for me to step into as the lead product engineer and start giving more specification, rounding out areas that aren't well defined with knowledge that I know about what we're trying to accomplish with the project, and then hand it back to TARS for execution.
zh: 这就给了我一个容易介入的框架,作为主导产品工程师开始给出更多规格说明,用我所知道的关于我们想用这个项目完成什么的知识,把定义不完善的区域补齐,然后再把它交回给 TARS 去执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's an example of the project.
zh: 这里有一个这个项目的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's, like I said, it sets up these first
zh: 就像我说的,它建立了这些最初

speaker: Unknown
en: milestones around our product engineering process.
zh: 围绕我们产品工程流程的里程碑。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we haven't done the Hilltop review yet here.
zh: 所以我们在这里还没做 Hilltop 评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: When that's done, we'll mark this ticket as complete, and TARS will pick that up and move on to the next stage of project implementation.
zh: 完成后，我们会把这个工单标记为完成，TARS 会接手并推进到项目实施的下一个阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we found is like a lot of teams are now doing more project brief and hilltop work because our agent can seed all that information.
zh: 我们发现，现在很多团队都在做更多的项目简报和山顶工作，因为我们的智能体可以填充所有这些信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's that blank page problem with writing.
zh: 这就是写作中的空白页问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can come into a document that already has information
zh: 如果你能进入一个已经有信息的文档

speaker: Unknown
en: And these agents aren't perfect.
zh: 而且这些智能体并不完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are times where it grossly overestimates what we're trying to accomplish with this project, and we have to cut out a lot of the scope that it comes up with.
zh: 有时候它会严重高估我们想通过这个项目实现的目标，我们不得不删掉它提出的很多范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's fine.
zh: 但这没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a lot simpler for an engineer to add input into rather than them spending time to set up all these primitives themselves.
zh: 对工程师来说，在已有基础上添加输入，比让他们花时间自己搭建所有这些基础组件要简单得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we can continue to drive this work through Slack, through Linear, and ultimately results in PRs in GitHub.
zh: 然后我们可以继续通过 Slack、Linear 推动这项工作，最终在 GitHub 上产生 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing that this lets us do is we don't necessarily always need to use our coding agent to implement pieces of work.
zh: 这样做的另一个好处是，我们不一定总是需要用我们的编码智能体来实现工作内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Devon is very popular.
zh: Devon 很受欢迎。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a lot of folks that really like using Devon.
zh: 我们有很多人非常喜欢使用 Devon。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can point Devon to these tickets and the same documentation to give Devon the context it needs to go and implement different parts of the work.
zh: 他们可以把 Devon 指向这些工单和同样的文档，给 Devon 提供它需要的上下文，去实现工作的不同部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same with the local Claude code, if you're just using Opus in a local harness.
zh: 本地的 Claude code 也是一样，如果你只是在本地环境里使用 Opus。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can grab through MCP all of these pieces of documentation and use that as context for its work.
zh: 它可以通过 MCP 获取所有这些文档，并将其作为它工作的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, we have people that collaborate in these project channels as well.
zh: 当然，也有人在这些项目频道中协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll notice our security team will come in and take a look at new projects, weigh in on the security implications and so forth.
zh: 你会注意到我们的安全团队会进来查看新项目，对安全影响等发表意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I alluded to early on in the development of our factory is created our own MCP gateway.
zh: 我之前提到过，在我们的工厂开发早期，我们创建了自己的 MCP 网关。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it our context engine.
zh: 我们称之为我们的上下文引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: This connects into all of our internal systems, but it also builds system prompts and context around how to navigate these tools and when to use these tools.
zh: 它连接到我们所有的内部系统，但它还会构建系统提示词和上下文，说明如何使用这些工具以及何时使用这些工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it is connected into Snowflake, which is our main data lake.
zh: 它连接到了 Snowflake，这是我们的主数据湖。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have semantic tables that we've built in Snowflake that describe product utilization or customer conversations.
zh: 我们在 Snowflake 中构建了语义表，描述产品使用情况或客户对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we can provide an agent through our MCP server in the tool description a list of here are the tables.
zh: 然后我们可以通过我们的 MCP 服务器在工具描述中向智能体提供一份列表：这些是表。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the content they
zh: 这是它们

speaker: Unknown
en: Contain.
zh: 包含的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're trying to answer questions about this type of content, write a query for these tables.
zh: 如果你想回答关于这类内容的问题，就为这些表编写查询。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it gives us a little bit of orientation to an agent to understand how we use our tools, how we've organized Linear and Snowflake, and give some guidance on where to find information.
zh: 所以它给智能体提供了一定的方向感，让它理解我们如何使用我们的工具，我们如何组织 Linear 和 Snowflake，并就去哪里找信息提供一些指导。

speaker: Unknown
en: What has been really surprising about this is we actually now use this MCP server across a lot of other different internal tools.
zh: 关于这一点真正令人惊讶的是，我们现在在很多其他内部工具中都使用这个 MCP 服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We open it up for people to query directly from Slack to do data or customer analysis.
zh: 我们把它开放给人们直接从 Slack 查询，做数据或客户分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so while we initially kind of
zh: 所以虽然我们最初

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: This has been an incredible piece of leverage for a lot of our internal teams.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to see that they're electing to move out of their local harness and into a cloud sandbox.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: We can see what's happening in the infrastructure.

speaker: Unknown
en: We use this information to self-improve the factory.

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted to learn.

speaker: Unknown
en: We wanted to get better about how it writes code.
zh: 我们想要在它如何写代码这方面做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to see where our engineers can improve their skills.
zh: 我们想看到我们的工程师可以在哪些方面提升他们的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much moving quickly in AI.
zh: AI 领域的变化太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of like a constant race to keep up with the latest tips and techniques.

speaker: Unknown
en: We can actually point agents at sessions and see where are the gaps in how people are using our factory.
